description: Third-party advertisers can analyze browsing data to create detailed profiles of individual users based on their browsing patterns, interests, and behaviors. This enables linking of data across different contexts and services.
assumptions: Browsing data contains sufficient behavioral information for profiling

title: Quasi-identifier identification through browsing patterns
description: Browsing data contains combinations of attributes (pages visited, timing, sequence) that can serve as quasi-identifiers to identify individual users, even without explicit identifiers.
assumptions: Browsing patterns are sufficiently unique to identify individuals

title: Dynamic set of third-party advertisers
description: Browsing data is shared with third-party advertisers who may form a dynamic set of parties that changes frequently, increasing exposure risk beyond what users may expect.
assumptions: Advertiser partnerships are not static and may change

title: Data propagation to external parties
description: Browsing data is propagated to third-party advertisers where it may be further processed, stored, or shared beyond the original purpose, creating additional privacy risks.
assumptions: Advertisers may share or process data beyond initial collection purpose

title: User unawareness of browsing data sharing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their browsing data is being collected by the AI recommendation engine and shared with third-party advertisers.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly disclose third-party data sharing

title: Lack of user control over data sharing preferences
description: Users may lack meaningful control to set preferences or consent regarding how their browsing data is shared with third-party advertisers.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may be limited or not granular

title: Invalid consent for third-party data sharing
description: Personal data collection and processing for sharing with third-party advertisers may not rely on valid, informed consent as required by GDPR and similar regulations.
assumptions: Consent may be bundled, not specific, or not freely given
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual consent implementation

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More browsing data may be processed and shared with advertisers than is actually needed for the recommendation functionality, violating data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Full browsing history may be shared when only aggregated data is needed

title: Linking through unique identifiers in transit
description: Browsing data transmitted in this flow may contain unique identifiers (cookies, device IDs, etc.) that enable linking of user data across different services and sessions.
assumptions: Identifiers are included in the browsing data payload

title: Processing of identified government ID data
description: Government ID images contain directly identified personal data (photos, names, ID numbers, dates of birth, addresses) that are stored in the file system. This constitutes processing of identified information.
assumptions: Government ID images contain standard identifying information

title: Unique identifiers in stored government IDs
description: Government ID images contain unique identifiers (ID numbers, biometric data) that directly reference the identity of data subjects. Storage in DS4 preserves these identifiers.
assumptions: Government IDs contain unique identification numbers

title: Revealing attributes in government ID images
description: Government ID images contain multiple revealing attributes (photo, name, DOB, address, ID number) that support identification of data subjects. All these attributes are stored together.
assumptions: Standard government ID format includes multiple identifying attributes

title: Linking through unique government ID identifiers
description: The unique identifiers in government ID images (ID numbers) stored in DS4 can be used to link this data with other data sources containing the same identifiers, enabling cross-system linking.
assumptions: Government ID numbers are used as identifiers across multiple systems

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: The combination of attributes in government ID images (photo, name, DOB, address) can serve as quasi-identifiers that enable linking even without explicit ID numbers.
assumptions: Attribute combinations in government IDs can uniquely identify individuals

title: Highly sensitive data type stored
description: Government ID images are highly sensitive personal data containing biometric and identification information. Storing full images may exceed what is functionally required if only specific fields are needed.
assumptions: Full image storage may be more than necessary for authentication purposes

title: Extended retention of government ID images
description: Government ID images may be stored in the file system longer than functionally necessary for authentication purposes, creating unnecessary privacy risk over time.
assumptions: Retention period may exceed functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about actual retention policy

title: Exposure to multiple parties via file system
description: Government ID images stored in a file system may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, depending on file system permissions and access controls.
assumptions: File system access may not be strictly limited to necessary parties
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual file system access controls

title: Data subject unawareness of government ID storage
description: Data subjects may not be fully aware that their government ID images are being stored in a file system, or the extent of this storage.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate image storage

title: Lack of control over government ID image erasure
description: Data subjects may lack control to request rectification or erasure of their government ID images stored in the file system.
assumptions: Data subject rights mechanisms may not be implemented for file system data

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Storing full government ID images may violate GDPR data minimization if only specific fields (not the full image) are needed for authentication functionality.
assumptions: Full image storage may exceed functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual authentication requirements

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: Government ID images may be stored longer than necessary for the stated purpose, violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.
assumptions: Retention period may not be clearly defined or limited
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual retention policy

title: JWT enables linking across sessions
description: JWT stored in localStorage contains user identifiers that can be used to link user activities across different sessions and potentially across different systems, creating persistent tracking capability.
assumptions: JWT contains user-identifying claims

title: JWT contains user identifier
description: The JWT stored in localStorage contains unique references to the identity of the data subject, enabling identification of the user from the stored token.
assumptions: JWT contains user identity claims

title: Sensitive authentication data stored in accessible location
description: JWTs contain authentication credentials which are sensitive data. Storing them in localStorage (accessible to JavaScript) exposes them to potential unauthorized access beyond what is functionally required.
assumptions: localStorage is accessible to page JavaScript

title: JWT may persist longer than needed
description: JWTs stored in localStorage persist until explicitly cleared, potentially longer than the authentication session requires, violating storage limitation principles.
assumptions: JWTs are not automatically cleared on logout or session end

title: Users unaware of JWT storage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their authentication tokens are being stored in browser localStorage, creating unawareness of processing.
assumptions: No explicit user notification about localStorage usage

title: Limited control over JWT removal
description: Users may lack easy mechanisms to rectify or erase JWTs stored in localStorage, limiting their control over personal data retention.
assumptions: No user interface for clearing authentication tokens

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: Storing JWTs in localStorage without automatic expiration or cleanup may violate GDPR storage limitation principle by retaining authentication data longer than necessary.
assumptions: JWTs persist beyond session lifetime
uncertainty_note: Depends on implementation of token expiration and cleanup

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management
description: Storing JWTs in localStorage is a known security vulnerability (XSS attacks can exfiltrate tokens), indicating insufficient cybersecurity risk management with privacy implications.
assumptions: No additional protections against XSS

title: Sensitive child history data disclosed
description: Child history data is inherently sensitive personal data. The process P3 shares this data with the parent, which may include sensitive information about the child's activities, behaviors, or development that could be perceived as highly sensitive.
assumptions: Child history data contains sensitive personal information about the child

title: Excessive volume of child history data
description: The process may retrieve and share an excessive amount of child history data beyond what is functionally needed for parent review, potentially including historical data that is no longer relevant.
assumptions: The system retrieves full child history rather than filtered or summarized data

title: Linking through quasi-identifiers in child history
description: Child history data may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., age, school, activities, dates) that could be combined to uniquely identify the child or link this data with other datasets about the child.
assumptions: Child history contains multiple attributes that could serve as quasi-identifiers

title: Revealing attributes in child history data
description: The child history data contains revealing attributes that support identification of the child data subject, such as specific activities, locations, or behavioral patterns.
assumptions: Child history includes specific identifying details about the child

title: Child unaware of data sharing with parent
description: The child data subject may not be aware that their history data is being shared with the parent for review, particularly if the child is young or if consent mechanisms are not age-appropriate.
assumptions: The child may not have been informed about this data sharing
uncertainty_note: Depends on age of child and consent mechanisms in place

title: Child lacks control over data sharing preferences
description: The child data subject may lack the ability to set preferences or consent regarding how their history data is processed and shared with the parent.
assumptions: Child has no mechanism to control or consent to data sharing
uncertainty_note: Depends on system design and age of child

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Sharing full child history data may violate GDPR data minimization principles if more data is processed than is actually needed for the parent review functionality.
assumptions: System shares more data than functionally necessary
uncertainty_note: Depends on what data is actually shared vs. what is needed

title: Invalid consent for child data processing
description: Processing and sharing child data may not rely on valid consent, particularly if the child is below the age of digital consent or if parental consent mechanisms are not properly implemented.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not be age-appropriate or properly implemented
uncertainty_note: Depends on age of child and consent implementation
